newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks end higher on improving sentiment.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks end higher on improving sentiment.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Saturday in active trading as sentiment improved on rising customer deposits with securities houses, brokers said.
"More and more investors are coming back," said Yoo Jae-kyong of Daishin Securities. "The impact of the Hanbo and Sammi failures has weakened."
The composite index closed 14.32 points higher at 667.19.

Customer deposits were estimated at around 3.2 trillion won, compared with 2.5 trillion loans for margin trading, brokers said. Talk that the government would act to revive the staggering economy helped boost sentiment.
Volume totalled 26.59 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 40.73 million on Friday.
Gainers outpaced losers 680 to 117 with 91 unchanged.
Brokers said financial shares soared on expectations that the government would accelerate reforms of the backward financial industry. The banking sub-index rose 5.39 percent to 349.48.
"A rebound for banks was anticipated because had been hit hardest by the collapse of Hanbo and Sammi," said a Hyundai Securities broker.
